meta.title: Mia's Photo Exhibition
meta.textType: story: a sequence with linking words

paragraphs: Mia took many photos of animals for the class blog. Teacher Kim liked them, so she said, "Let us make an exhibition in the school library." "Can I use the big wall?" asked Mia. "Yes," said Teacher Kim. "It starts on Friday." Mia had only two days, and she began at once.

First, Mia looked at one hundred photos on her tablet. She chose twelve of them. She did not choose the most beautiful photos. She chose the photos with the best stories. Her favorite was a photo of her white kitten, Snow, on a red chair. She put the twelve photos in a blue folder. Then she took the folder to the library.

But the printer was not available on Wednesday morning. Another class used it for a test. Mia looked at the clock many times. "Do you need help?" asked Leo. "Yes, please," said Mia. After that, Mia waited until lunch. At last, the printer was free, and she printed all twelve photos. Lily and May helped her put them up on the wall.

Next, Leo made an advertisement for the exhibition. He drew a big camera and wrote, "MIA'S ANIMALS, FRIDAY, IN THE LIBRARY." He put it on the board near the school gate. "Now everybody can see it," he said.

Early on Friday, the library was quiet and clean. The twelve photos looked small on the big wall. Mia walked around the room two times. Then she wanted one last photo of the room. She lifted her camera, but the battery was dead. "Oh no!" she said. Lily gave her an extra battery from her bag. "Why do you carry an extra battery?" asked Mia. "I always carry one for the blog," said Lily. Mia took the photo, and Lily looked pleased.

Finally, the exhibition opened at ten o'clock. Teacher Kim stood at the door and welcomed each child. Many children came to the library, and a few teachers came too. Mia stood next to her kitten photo and answered their questions. They stopped at each photo and read the small cards. That evening, Mia received an email from Nadia, her friend in Singapore. It said, "Dear Mia, I saw your photos on the blog. The kitten is my favorite. Best wishes, Nadia." Mia read it two times and smiled.
text.summary: Mia makes an exhibition of her animal photos in the school library. She chooses the photos, prints them, and puts them up, and then Nadia sends her an email.
